simple.meaning: זִמְרָן (Zimrân) is a Hebrew word meaning “Zimran , a son of Abraham by Keturah.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: זִמְרָן (H2175) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Genesis 25:2, with occurrences in Genesis, 1 Chronicles.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to זִמְרָן (H2175) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in זִמְרָן (H2175) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: זִמְרָן (Zimrân) / H2175 is traced through Genesis 25:2, 1 Chronicles 1:32 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: Zimran , a son of Abraham by Keturah
definitions.full: H2175. Zimran זִמְרָן proper name, masculine son of Abraham & Keturah , ᵐ5 Ζε ( μ ) βραν Gen 25:2 and 1Chr 1:32 ( ᵐ5 L here Ζεμραμ ). On locality referred to see Di.

occurrences.englishText: She bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
The sons of Keturah, Abraham’s concubine: she bore Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. The sons of Jokshan: Sheba and Dedan.
